The program is also a great experience for students who are learning English because it provides another way to build confidence in speaking, learn new words and phrases in a playful manner, and, of course, develop bonds with classmates while exploring new artistic approaches.[/vc_column_text][/toggle][toggle color=”Default” heading_tag=”default” heading_tag_functionality=”default” title=”Will lunch be provided?”][vc_column_text]Lunch will not be provided for the summer program. If it’s something that would benefit you and your family, please email us expressing your interest and needs so we can consider it for future programs.[/vc_column_text][/toggle][toggle color=”Default” heading_tag=”default” heading_tag_functionality=”default” title=”Do you offer scholarships?”][vc_column_text]Yes! We believe every child should have access to the arts, regardless of financial circumstances.

We offer full scholarships funded in part by The Children’s Trust for qualifying families. Miami New Drama’s Summer Theater Intensive is funded in part by The Children’s Trust. The Children’s Trust is a dedicated source of revenue established by voter referendum to improve the lives of children and families in Miami-Dade County.

In addition, we offer partial scholarships funded by Miami New Drama for families who may not meet the requirements for a full scholarship but still need support. Our goal is to make sure every young artist has the opportunity to participate and thrive.

When filling out the registration form, just check off that you are interested in applying for a scholarship and the form will help you through the next steps.[/vc_column_text][/toggle][toggle color=”Default” heading_tag=”default” heading_tag_functionality=”default” title=”Is there a sibling discount?”][vc_column_text]If you do not qualify for scholarships, please email us about interest in a sibling discount. [/vc_column_text][/toggle][toggle color=”Default” heading_tag=”default” heading_tag_functionality=”default” title=”Does my student have to audition?”][vc_column_text]Rather than holding formal auditions, we observe students throughout the process as they grow and engage in class through a variety of exercises. This helps our teaching artists understand each student’s strengths and interests more holistically. All of our shows incorporate a collaborative creation component, meaning every student is guaranteed a role in the final performance.[/vc_column_text][/toggle][toggle color=”Default” heading_tag=”default” heading_tag_functionality=”default” title=”I’m not sure if my child likes theater or will want to pursue it as a career. Is this program still suitable?”][vc_column_text]Definitely! MiND programs are designed to emphasize creative exploration and personal growth rather than professional preparation. Every child is welcomed as a co-creator and leaves with skills in confidence, collaboration, critical thinking, and the ability to develop teamwork skills to achieve collective success —tools that are useful and applicable in any path they choose, beyond the arts.[/vc_column_text][/toggle][toggle color=”Default” heading_tag=”default” heading_tag_functionality=”default” title=”My child has never participated in theater before—can they still join the program?”][vc_column_text]Yes! No prior experience is necessary. Our intensives are designed for all skill levels and adapted to meet each participant where they are. We focus on building a strong foundation in a fun and supportive environment. This year, we will have two groups: one for advanced students and another for new students. This allows us to better support each participant—students with prior experience can encounter new challenges and opportunities for artistic growth, while newer students have the time and space to explore and develop new skills.[/vc_column_text][/toggle][/toggles][/vc_column][/vc_row]

” font_container=”tag:h3|text_align:left|color:%2374d1ea|line_height:1.5″ use_theme_fonts=”yes”][divider line_type=”Full Width Line” line_thickness=”1″ divider_color=”default” animate=”yes” custom_height=”40″][vc_column_text]About the Play: Cosmic Curiosity

Cosmic Curiosity brings to life the story of Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz, a 17th-century Mexican nun, poet, and scholar whose love for learning defied expectations. At a time when education for women was rare, she pursued knowledge with determination, becoming one of the most influential literary figures of her era.

This engaging play blends Sor Juana’s writings with imagined moments from her daily life, exploring her intellectual journey, her decision to enter the convent, and the challenges she faced. Cosmic Curiosity captures an era when poets, scientists, and philosophers were shaping the world through discovery and debate.

Written and directed by Carmen Peláez, a Miami-based award-winning playwright, actress, and director (Fake, The Cuban Vote, Rum & Coke). She is a 2023 MacDowell Fellow, Ellie Award recipient, and HBO NYLFF Short Film Competition winner. As a dedicated teaching artist, she helps young people develop their own plays.

About the Tour

A small ensemble of professional actors will bring Cosmic Curiosity to schools, making Sor Juana’s story engaging and accessible. Through historical texts and theatrical storytelling, the play explores her unconventional education, her path to becoming a writer, and her lasting influence.

Audiences will follow her journey from a self-taught child prodigy to the first Hispanic woman to publish a book in Spain, building a library of 4,000 books. Once nearly forgotten, she is now celebrated as a literary icon, even appearing on the 100 Mexican peso bill.

With humor, drama, and poetry, Cosmic Curiosity highlights a woman whose passion for learning still inspires today.

Talkback & Educational Resources

All performances will be followed by a talkback session, providing students and educators an opportunity to engage in deeper discussions. Supporting materials will be provided to enhance classroom discussions before and after the show. Topics may include:

  • Life in 17th-century Mexico and the role of education
  • Sor Juana’s influences and contributions to literature
  • The role of curiosity in learning and discovery, especially as a driving force across disciplines
  • The new ideas and developments emerging regarding literature, philosophy, and science.

For questions, comments, or requests to tour to your school, please contact our Department of Education.

custom_height=”40″][vc_column_text]The Courage (To Right a Woman’s Wrongs), a Spanish Golden Age comedy by Ana Caro de Mallén y Soto and directed by Peter Romano, a Syrian-American musician and teaching artist with an MFA from Columbia University and BFA from NYU Tisch School of the Arts.

Six professional actors will be bringing to our century The Courage to Right a Woman’s Wrongs, a witty critique of society through the story of Leonor, a woman who sets out to find her one-time lover (Don Juan, naturally) and bring him to justice. The play is a comedy of wild intrigue and lively ingenuity in which Leonor crosses geographical boundaries and defies social expectations of gender in order to bring her fickle lover to justice and restore her lost honor.

The author, Ana Caro de Mallén y Soto (ca.1601–ca.1645), was a Spanish poet and playwright. Born an enslaved person in Granada, Spain, she came to be one of the most celebrated playwrights of Spain’s Golden Age. This adaption, translated by UCLA’s academics, was created by Miami-based playwright, actress, director Maria Corina Ramirez, is available to tour Miami-Dade County public schools.

All performances will be followed by a talkback where topics such as the following can be addressed: Comedia of the Hispanic golden age, overcoming the Don Juan myth, female solidarity, courtship practices, cross-dressing, and theater within the theater.

For questions, comments, or requests to tour to your school, please contact our Department of Education.

  • Creative Writing (virtual) – Everybody has a story to tell! A virtual camp dedicated to spark the creative process and learn the basic principles of writing and dramaturgy. Participants will be guided through exercises to learn tips on how to turn their ideas and thoughts into dialogue, conflict, and a resolution within a scene or short play. We will be bringing professional writers as special guests to give you all their amazing tips and tricks!
  • Acting for the Camera (bilingual, virtual) – Explore different on-camera acting techniques that will help you develop your potential as a bilingual actor. Learn with industry professionals about headshots, how to prepare for auditions, and everything you need to step into the world of entertainment in English and Spanish.​

Brecht believed that we should treat the Theatre as a laboratory. He emphasized having an objective distance between observer and actor, to remind the audience that what they are witnessing is, in fact, an illusion. Doing so allows an audience to watch how an event unfolds, and what decisions the characters make that lead there. We invited our audiences to examine this story, we asked that they judge the morality of the characters and their decisions, and we hope we taught them something about what it means to be a human being in this world.

The Caucasian Chalk Circle is about love without respite. A young woman fights against the effects of a corrupted society to save the life of a child. During a revolution, Grusha, a house maid, picks up a baby that is left behind by the royal family. She nurtures this child as though it were her own. Grusha journeys up a mountain, crosses a broken bridge, evades malicious soldiers and eventually loses her fiancé because of her commitment to the child. Staring in the face of all of the obstacles Brecht presents, Grusha chooses to do good despite what it costs her. Brecht teaches us the true meaning of courage and asks us to follow Grusha’s example — to be radically humane in the face of an inhumane world.

Formado con grandes directores como Juan Carlos Gené, Enrique Porte, Levy Rosell y Ugo Ulive. Basilio Álvarez se ha convertido en uno de los referentes principales dentro del teatro venezolano, no solo como actor sino también como director, teniendo en su haber más de 40 montajes teatrales dirigidos tanto con su grupo “Skena” como con otros grupos productores de gran prestigio. Ha recibido los premios teatrales más importantes en venezuela: el Marco Antonio Ettedgui, el Premio Nacional casa del artista y en varias oportunidades ha sido reconocido por los premios municipales de Caracas como mejor actor, productor y director, así como también el Ministerio de la Cultura lo ha distinguido con las órdenes mérito al trabajo en bronce y plata. Entre sus trabajos más destacados como actor recordamos su participación en los montajes de: Esperando a Godot, Art, La cena de los idiotas, El dia que me quieras, La revolución, Ay Carmela, La Ola, Hamlet, Chicago, Enemigo del pueblo, I.D.I.O.T.A., y su última e impactante actuación como Rothko en la versión venezolana de “Rojo” de John Logan. Basilio Álvarez se desempeña también como dramaturgo y escritor no sólo de obras de teatro juveniles e infantiles, sino también de telenovelas y seriados para television con Radio Caracas Televisión en Venezuela, Telemundo en USA, R.T.I. en Colombia, TELEVISA y ARGOS en México. column_border_style=”solid”][vc_column_text css=”.vc_custom_1632758389370{margin-top: 30px !important;margin-bottom: 30px !important;}”]Esta sesión será dirigida por Mariana Araoz, directora y pedagoga argentina-venezolana-francesa, ahora residente en París, dedicada al arte de la Máscara y la Marioneta por 30 años.

Ella creó el “Método del Equilibrio-TMR” inspirado en pedagogos como Mario Gonzalez (Théâtre du soleil), Jacques Lecoq, Delphine Eliet, Barbara Wilczek Ekholm (Directora del Conservatorio Nacional de Malmo, Suecia) así como en el teatro tradicional de marioneta y máscara como Bunraku, Kabuki, Teatro Noh y Butto.

El método se basa en el concepto de equilibrio del espacio teatral, los actores y el grupo actoral como eje de creatividad. A través del método se logra la transmisión de emociones y conocimientos entre un miembro del grupo y otro creando una historia común. Los “sirvientes del escenario” (como en el teatro oriental) y los “actores-marioneta”(Meyerhold)  le dan vida a los personajes y a la historia. Araoz ha creado con su método una forma de contar historias con el ejercicio creativo llamado: El vuelo de los Pájaros.

La respiración, la postura, la precisión, el estar consciente, alerta, presente, y sobre todo el apoyo y la buena mirada del grupo son la base de este trabajo.

Mariana Araoz, directora argentina-venezolana-francesa, actriz y pedagoga especializada en Teatro de Máscaras y Marionetas. Nacida en Buenos Aires, vivió en Venezuela, Canadá y Alemania. Llega a Francia a la edad de 22 años. Recibe su maestría en Ecología de la Universidad de Rennes II y una licenciatura en estudios teatrales de la Sorbona. Es discípula de Mario González (Theater du Soleil) por más de 20 años.

Crea en 2004 la Compañía Collectif Masque junto con Christophe Patty y Etienne Champion y en 2006 crea el proyecto entre Suecia y Francia : “Trans Mission Research (TMR)” basado en el equilibrio de género y las máscaras.  Es de esta investigación y fruto de su encuentro activo entre el teatro social y los conceptos de equilibrio del teatro sueco que nace el “Método del equilibrio – TMR.”

Como directora ha producido más de 40 puestas en Suecia, Francia y Estados Unidos. En Estados Unidos ha dirigido en Minneapolis en el Guthrie Lab y en Chicago en el Art Center. En Suecia, ha dirigido en teatros nacionales y regionales  siendo en el 2014 nominada para el Premio Thalia por su puesta en escena de “La Gaviota” de Chekhov en el Skillinge Teater. En Francia fue galardonada el premio “Avignon-Off” en el 2017 por la obra “Disección de una nevada.”.  El Panteón de París ha seleccionado su última creación “Misión Invisible” en Francia.

Como pedagoga, Mariana es profesora permanente en la Escuela Nacional de Malmö, en Suecia y en “Ecole de Jeu” en París, así como profesora asociada en el Conservatorio Nacional de Arte dramático de París, Universidad de Columbia (Nueva York), Carlton College (Northfield), el Instituto Boris Schoukin (Moscú) y el Instituto Nacional de Teatro (Hong Kong). Ha enseñado como invitada académica en St. Olaf College en Minneapolis (2002-2012).[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][/vc_row]

Theatre of Harlem, Carl Cofield, for some insight into directing the classics. Previous direction with Miami New Drama includes Kemp Power’s One Night in Miami. Taking a look at Euripides’ The Bacchae, he breaks down how one can begin to reimagine these texts. How does one make these plays just as relevant for today’s theatre audiences? What can YOU, as the director, bring to the retelling of these stories? Carl will be answering this and much more.

Carl Cofield is a New York based director, actor and is currently the Associate Artistic Director of the Classical Theatre of Harlem.  He directed the award winning world premiere of One Night In Miami (Huffington Post best of L.A. 2013, N.A.A.C.P., L.A. Drama Critics Circle and others) for Rogue Machine Theater and the Denver Center Theatre, for which, he received the Los Angeles N.A.A.C.P award for Best Director. Twelfth Night  for Yale Rep, Radio Golf for Everyman, Disgraced for The Denver Center and Henry IV part 2 for the Oregon Shakespeare Festival, A Raisin In the Sun for Two River Theater Company, The Mountaintop for Cleveland Play House.  NYC directing credits include: The Bacchae and  Antigone for the Classical Theatre of Harlem, the 50th anniversary of Dutchman for the Classical Theatre of Harlem/National Black Theatre, The Tempest, Macbeth for Classical Theatre of Harlem, The Balcony  ​(The New School), Better Than Yellow for 48 Hours In Harlem, The Seven by Will Power at the Connelly Theatre, A Midsummer Night’s Dream for N.Y.U,  1001, for Columbia University, The Tuskegee Airman Project for CUNY York College. He assisted Molly Smith in the world premiere of Camp David by Laurence Wright at Arena Stage. He directed the reading of Camp David for President and First Lady Carter at the Carter Center retreat in Vail, Colorado. He also assisted Kent Gash on Langston In Harlem at Urban Stages.

As an actor, his work has been seen at The Manhattan Theater Club (Ruined), Berkeley Rep, Alliance, Arena Stage, The Shakespeare Theater, Intiman, Actors Theater of Louisville, Shakespeare Santa Cruz, Milwaukee Rep, Alabama Shakespeare, The McCarter, The Acting Company, The Studio Theatre and many others.

Dionne Figgins began her career as a member of Dance Theatre of Harlem, under the direction of Arthur Mitchell, dancing lead roles in Serenade, Four Temperaments, Agon, and Concerto Barocco.  She also appeared as a guest artist with Complexions Contemporary Ballet. Broadway credits include Hot Feet, Memphis, Leap of Faith, and Motown the Musical.  Regional/Off-Broadway credits include Trip of Love, Chicago, and Smokey Joe’s Café.  Film/TV credits include Power, Flesh and Bone (Yasmine), Bolden.  She is the co-founder of Broadway Serves, a non-profit organization whose mission is to connect theater professionals to community service opportunities.  Proud member of AEA/SAG.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column_inner][vc_column_inner column_padding=”padding-3-percent” column_padding_tablet=”inherit” column_padding_phone=”inherit” column_padding_position=”all” column_element_spacing=”default” background_color_opacity=”1″ background_hover_color_opacity=”1″ column_shadow=”none” column_border_radius=”none” column_link_target=”_self” gradient_direction=”left_to_right” overlay_strength=”0.3″ width=”1/2″ tablet_width_inherit=”default” bg_image_animation=”none” border_type=”simple” column_border_width=”none” column_border_style=”solid”][image_with_animation image_url=”7071″ animation=”Fade In” hover_animation=”none” alignment=”center” border_radius=”none” box_shadow=”small_depth” image_loading=”default” max_width=”100%” max_width_mobile=”default”][/vc_column_inner][/vc_row_inner][/vc_column][/vc_row]
